Thanks Karthik — we reviewed the MSA + Order Form and have two sticking points from legal/procurement: 1) your Limitation of Liability is too broad relative to our prepaid fees (they want a full refund option on termination for convenience) and 2) the wind-down assistance language is vague. Attached is ACME's counter redline (see section called 'Refunds & Operational Exit').

High level asks from our side:
- If we terminate for convenience within the first 12 months, we want a pro rata refund of unused prepaid fees OR funds held in escrow;
- LoL should not bar recovery for direct transition costs (third-party vendor fees to migrate) or for breaches that cause data loss;
- Wind-down assistance: 30 days of support or compensation to cover integration rollback.

Can Redwood confirm willingness to: limit LoL to aggregate fees paid in prior 12 months EXCEPT for (i) indemnity, (ii) willful misconduct, (iii) damages arising from data loss/breach; and provide a defined wind-down SOW/credit?

—Ben

Ben — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Lauren (legal) and Neha (sales ops) to coordinate. Quick answers up front:
- We can agree to a defined refund mechanism for prepaid fees on a convenience termination, but we need a carve that prevents a refund claim that exceeds fees actually paid under the Order Form (and we want to limit retroactive claims).
- For LoL, Redwood's baseline position is an aggregate cap equal to the fees paid in the preceding 12 months; exceptions for indemnity and gross negligence/willful misconduct are standard. We're open to a narrowly tailored carve for direct, documented transition costs (e.g., third-party migration costs) but not broad consequential damage carve-outs.
- Wind-down assistance: we typically provide 30 days of operational support or a credit equal to the remaining prepaid value, and we'll supply a short SOW appendix.

Lauren / Neha — please review ACME's redline and suggest precise contractual language we can propose back (I want something we can send to Ben today). Key risk areas to flag: open-ended consequential carveouts, uncapped refund claims, and ambiguous definition of 'transition costs'.

Thanks,

Quick legal take after reading ACME's doc:

1) Proposed language for Section 6 (Limitation of Liability):
- "Except for (i) liability arising from Redwood's indemnity obligations; (ii) liability resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; and (iii) liability for loss or compromise of Customer Data caused by Redwood's breach, the aggregate liability of Redwood for any and all claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees actually paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form during the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim."

2) Transition / wind-down carve: define 'Transition Costs' narrowly to mean "reasonable third-party costs actually incurred to migrate Customer Data out of Redwood's platform within thirty (30) days following termination, excluding internal headcount or opportunity costs." Limit recovery to documented invoices and aggregate cap equal to remaining prepaid fees.

3) Refund for convenience termination: offer pro rata refund based on unused months of the prepaid term, net of any non-refundable setup fees and outstanding invoices. Add a short exhibit to the Order Form that calculates the refund formula.

4) Consequential damages: keep exclusion language but add an explicit exception for damages arising from data loss or unauthorized data disclosure (i.e., maintain carve for data breach).

I attached a PDF with the redline text for Section 6 and a draft short 'Wind-Down SOW' we can attach to the Order Form. My preference: send ACME a tracked-change redline that replaces ACME's sweeping refund request with a precise pro rata + documented transition cost option.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Order Form redlines — prepaid escrow, LoL carve-outs and wind-down ops

Ben — attaching suggested language from our counsel and a 1-page wind-down SOW. High level compromise we're proposing:
- LoL cap = fees paid in prior 12 months; carve-outs: indemnity, willful misconduct/gross negligence, and data-loss damages;
- For termination for convenience within the prepaid term: pro rata refund of unused months, excluding non-refundable setup charges; refunds calculated as (remaining months / total prepaid months) * prepaid amount;
- Transition costs: customer may recover documented third-party migration costs up to remaining prepaid amount; Redwood requires invoices and prior written approval for any third-party spend > $10k;
- We will also offer a 30-day operational handoff (docs + 8 hours of hands-on support) as standard; if Customer needs additional runbook/onsite support, that will be scoped via the Wind-Down SOW and billed or deducted from the remaining prepaid balance.

If this sounds reasonable, we'll send a tracked-change version of the MSA + Order Form. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the formulas and the approval process for transition vendors.

Thanks,
Karthik
[Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_Redline_v2.docx (docx)]

Karthik / Lauren — appreciate the fast turnaround and the concrete language. Our legal team reviewed your proposed Section 6 and the Wind-Down SOW. Two quick clarifications before we accept:

1) Can you change the refund formula to allow refunding any prepayments held in escrow immediately on termination (rather than waiting for a 30-day reconciliation)? We want faster access to escrowed funds for procurement accounting.

2) Regarding third-party transition costs: ACME is willing to require pre-approval for >$10k, but we ask that Redwood agrees not to unreasonably withhold approval and to respond to vendor approval requests within 3 business days.

If you can accept those two quick edits, legal is ready to sign the Order Form and we'll route to procurement for final signature.

—Ben
